<section class="story-intro">
<p class="eyebrow">Real city data · four-step calculation · observable feedback</p>
<h1>From city activity<br>to <em>road flows.</em></h1>
<p class="lede">One GMNS-based data and computation framework, two primary cases. Central Boston connects four stages, transit observations and saved static assignment methods to real roads. Classical Sioux Falls exposes separate static assignment and historical space–time experiments without inventing real-city GPS data.</p>

<div class="wrap"><section id="gmns-in-action"><p class="eyebrow">One network reference for zones, demand, observations and results</p><div class="sectionhead"><h2>GMNS in Action</h2><p>Actual Boston objects retain separate identities while documented keys connect H3 zones, modeled access, physical roads and saved evidence. This shared data foundation is not a fifth model stage.</p></div><figure class="figure-tile boston-feature"><a href="datasets/boston-gmns-exchange.md#one-network-multiple-connected-data-layers"><img src="assets/boston/gmns_in_action_r1/gmns_connected_layers.png" alt="Real Boston zone 35 and zonal OD, centroid and dashed nonphysical access connector, physical road access, plus a separate GPS-link-result relationship."></a><figcaption><b>Separate objects, explicit relationships.</b>Model access connectors are not physical roads. Shared link references do not imply a shared observed trip. <a href="datasets/boston-gmns-exchange.md">Read the exact records and profile →</a></figcaption></figure><p>The pinned GMNS Plus Level 2 reader accepted both S1 and S2 node/link/demand sets; the zone schema was checked separately. The declared <code>mcl_solver_*</code> extensions preserve the accepted physical solver inputs through a reversible adapter. These are structural and round-trip checks, not new matching or improved prediction.</p><div class="actions"><a class="button primary" href="datasets/boston-gmns-exchange.md#reproduce-the-relationships">Run the read-only relationship lookup →</a><a class="button" href="../examples/boston/gmns_exchange_r1/README.md">Open the exchange files →</a></div></section></div>
<div class="soft"><div class="wrap"><section id="four-step-workflow">
<div class="sectionhead"><h2>Four stages.<br>Actual saved results.</h2><p>The figures below show model outputs, not just map layers. Inputs, calculations and interpretation are linked at every step.</p></div>
<div class="four-step-cards">
<article class="stage-card" id="stage-1"><div class="stage-copy"><p class="eyebrow">01 · Trip Generation</p><h3>Households become trip productions.</h3><p>Area-allocated ACS households × transferred regional rates, with activity-based attraction weights.</p><strong class="result-line">816,054.67 modeled workday person trips</strong></div><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-1-trip-generation"><img src="assets/boston/four_step_results_r1/step1_generation.png" alt="Actual saved zonal production totals grouped by six purpose codes."></a><div class="stage-footer"><p>Regional mean-rate transfer, not an observed local trip count.</p><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-1-trip-generation">Inputs → calculation → productions</a></div></article>
<article class="stage-card" id="stage-2"><div class="stage-copy"><p class="eyebrow">02 · Trip Distribution</p><h3>Productions become OD demand.</h3><p>Gravity/IPF and purpose/time-specific direction conversion distribute trips between H3 zones.</p><strong class="result-line">177 × 177 HBW midday OD matrix</strong></div><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-2-trip-distribution"><img src="assets/boston/four_step_results_r1/step2_distribution.png" alt="Saved modeled HBW midday origin-destination matrix."></a><div class="stage-footer"><p>22,807.22 modeled midday person trips. Not GPS-derived passenger OD.</p><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-2-trip-distribution">Margins → impedance → OD</a></div></article>
<article class="stage-card" id="stage-3"><div class="stage-copy"><p class="eyebrow">03 · Mode Choice</p><h3>Service costs change mode shares.</h3><p>Scheduled and adjusted transit journeys drive a nested response around regional baseline shares.</p><strong class="result-line">4.0990% → 4.2246% walk-access transit</strong></div><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-3-mode-choice"><img src="assets/boston/four_step_results_r1/step3_mode_response.png" alt="Saved percentage-point mode response for panel_od_019 at 12:30."></a><div class="stage-footer"><p>One case, μ_transit = 1. S1 is not an OD-specific absolute-cost baseline.</p><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-3-mode-choice">Itinerary costs → probability → person demand</a></div></article>
<article class="stage-card" id="stage-4"><div class="stage-copy"><p class="eyebrow">04 · Traffic Assignment</p><h3>Vehicle demand becomes road flow.</h3><p>The same static FW solver loads the eligible private/occupied-vehicle panel onto the common network.</p><strong class="result-line">202.078384 → 202.070733 vehicle trips</strong></div><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-4-traffic-assignment"><img src="assets/boston/visual_release_r1/boston_panel_flow_s1.png" alt="Saved S1 modeled panel vehicle flow on Central Boston roads."></a><div class="stage-footer"><p>Fixed panel without regional background traffic—not citywide measured congestion.</p><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-4-traffic-assignment">Vehicle OD → FW → directed-link flow</a></div></article>
</div>
<div class="scope-bridge"><b>One linked workflow; deliberately different scopes.</b><p>Regional generation → HBW demand → 36 selected OD pairs × 3 midday departures → 78 eligible OD–time cases → the vehicle-assignment panel. The full regional total is not loaded to roads. Thirty incomplete cases keep their demand and exclusion records.</p></div>
<div class="actions"><a class="button primary" href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md">Read the complete four-step result →</a><a class="button" href="datasets/boston-four-step-sources.md">Download plot data and provenance →</a></div>
</section></div></div>
<div class="wrap"><section id="gps-feedback" class="gps-story">
<p class="eyebrow">Not just a map of points</p><div class="sectionhead"><h2>What does GPS<br>actually change?</h2><p>It changes a transit service-time input. The dependent journey costs, mode demand and road-flow response are then recomputed—not the regional trip total.</p></div>
<div class="feedback-chain" aria-label="GPS feedback dependency"><div><small>Observe</small><b>Vehicle position<br>and service interval</b></div><span>→</span><div><small>Estimate an input</small><b>Interval-time<br>adjustment</b></div><span>→</span><div><small>Stage 03</small><b>Transit cost<br>and mode response</b></div><span>→</span><div><small>Stage 04</small><b>Vehicle demand<br>and road flows</b></div></div>
<div class="feedback-case"><div><span class="tag">One actual saved trace</span><h3>Route 749 · direction 1</h3><p>Stop pair 1788 → 5093 has <strong>86 s sample-derived elapsed time versus 180 s planned</strong>. Its declared interval adjustment changes the saved result for <code>panel_od_019</code> at 12:30.</p><p class="note">The adjustment is retrospective and exploratory. All 13 interval factors are off by default, each supported by one event. It is not an independently validated forecast.</p></div><div class="tablewrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Same OD–departure</th><th>S1</th><th>S2</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Transit time</td><td>29.052 min</td><td>27.486 min</td></tr><tr><td>Fare</td><td>$1.70</td><td>$1.70</td></tr><tr><td>Walk-access transit</td><td>4.0990%</td><td>4.2246%</td></tr><tr><td>Vehicle trips</td><td>2.164631</td><td>2.161796</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div>
<figure class="figure-tile boston-feature"><a href="datasets/boston-gmns-exchange.md#from-gps-coordinates-to-gmns-linked-evidence"><img src="assets/boston/gmns_in_action_r1/gps_to_gmns_evidence.png" alt="Same twelve route-60 saved source positions in identical before and after map bounds, then ordered path-link and saved modeled road-result lookup."></a><figcaption><b>Before → after → inspect.</b>The source positions are unchanged; the saved algorithm-derived path and projections give them physical-link references. A separate modeled S1 result can be queried by link ID. This qualified route-60 segment is not the route-749 feedback event above. <a href="datasets/boston-gmns-exchange.md#from-gps-coordinates-to-gmns-linked-evidence">Check the keys, units and limits →</a></figcaption></figure>
<div class="visual-grid"><figure class="figure-tile"><a href="datasets/boston-central.md#one-saved-transit-position-projection"><img src="assets/boston/visual_release_r1/boston_gps_projection.png" alt="A separate recorded segment illustrates GPS positions projected onto matched road reference lines."></a><figcaption><b>First, establish the spatial link.</b>The original projection map uses a different recorded segment. It illustrates road matching, not the exact event in the numeric trace above.</figcaption></figure><figure class="figure-tile"><a href="datasets/boston-behavior-feedback.md#step-4-traffic-assignment"><img src="assets/boston/visual_release_r1/boston_panel_flow_delta.png" alt="Saved aggregate S2 minus S1 fixed-panel flow differences; maximum absolute change about 0.006603 vehicle trips."></a><figcaption><b>Then, inspect the model response.</b>78 links differ; maximum |Δ| ≈ 0.006603 panel vehicle trips. Link totals combine multiple OD cases, not just the one illustrated trace.</figcaption></figure></div>
<p class="focus-note"><strong>Switch it off and verify the connection.</strong> Srestore independently disables the overlay and recomputes service costs, probabilities and demand, returning the comparable results to S1. This verifies a computational dependency, not empirical accuracy. GPS does not estimate the regional total, gravity β or all passenger OD in this example.</p>

</section></div>

<div class="soft"><div class="wrap"><section id="gmns-foundation"><div class="sectionhead"><h2>GMNS foundation and toolchain alignment</h2><p>Open the same Boston roads, H3 zones, hierarchy and zonal vehicle demand as a versioned exchange, then trace their links to the saved four-stage and GPS results.</p></div><p>177 fine-zone centroids retain separate identities even when they share one of 139 physical access nodes. <div class="wrap"><section id="boston-case" class="case-section">
<p class="eyebrow">Case 01 · real-city modelled panel</p><div class="sectionhead"><h2>Boston: four stages, GPS and saved assignment methods.</h2><p>GMNS physical link identity and its documented export crosswalk let different assignment outputs return to the same roads without changing the older semantic S1 demand.</p></div>
<p>The four-stage/GPS story above is the accepted semantic S1/S2 example (about <b>202.078384 / 202.070733</b> modelled vehicle trips). A separate conditional absolute-attribute DA/S2/S3/TW sensitivity evaluated 87 of 108 fixed objects (21 unknown); 78 common objects were road-loaded. Its <b>ABS_PLANNED</b> algorithm comparison freezes 5,091 physical links, 26 endpoint OD pairs, 203.6604786350987 modelled vehicle trips and one 130-path pool. <a href="cases/boston.md">Full Boston case, stages and source boundaries →</a></p>
<div class="tablewrap"><table><thead><tr><th>ABS_PLANNED saved method</th><th>Original Beckmann F · vehicle-minutes</th><th>Original-space diagnostic</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><a href="../examples/boston/assignment_methods_r1/reference/fw_solution.csv">FW</a></td><td>707.0579230712884</td><td>Saved static network result</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="../examples/boston/assignment_methods_r1/reference/full_path_flow.csv">Uncompressed SLSQP · 130 paths</a></td><td>707.0579230712882</td><td>Saved exact finite-pool OD equalities</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="../examples/boston/assignment_methods_r1/runs/rank26/outer_02_check.json">Native Diagnostic L3 · rank 26 · outer 02</a></td><td>707.0578811137339</td><td>Max OD 8.255328278750085e-7; signed relative gap <b>−5.933966773022305e-8</b>; 52 path coordinates / 5,143 total native variables</td></tr>
<tr><td><a href="../examples/boston/assignment_methods_r1/runs/rank52/outer_02_check.json">Native Diagnostic L3 · rank 52 · outer 02</a></td><td>707.0578811562873</td><td>Max OD 8.254705861077127e-7; signed relative gap <b>−5.927948547394401e-8</b>; 78 path coordinates / 5,169 total native variables</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
<p class="note">The native points pass recorded numerical checks, but their negative gaps reflect tolerated OD deficits, not exact feasible equilibria or improved traffic. Their initialization reused the full-path reference; no cold-start acceleration or peak IPOPT memory is claimed. ABS_OBS_EXPLORATORY is a separate FW scenario with 203.6573680559407 trips and F=707.043586277782.</p>
<div class="assignment-grid"><figure class="figure-tile"><a href="cases/boston-assignment.md#physical-link-flow-maps"><img src="assets/boston/assignment_methods_r1/boston_abs_planned_fw_flow.png" alt="Saved Boston ABS_PLANNED FW physical-link flow with common scale."></a><figcaption><b>FW · ABS_PLANNED</b>Saved physical-link volume.</figcaption></figure><figure class="figure-tile"><a href="cases/boston-assignment.md#physical-link-flow-maps"><img src="assets/boston/assignment_methods_r1/boston_abs_planned_l3_rank26_flow.png" alt="Accepted native L3 rank-26 reconstructed physical-link flow with same scale."></a><figcaption><b>Native L3 · rank 26</b>Outer-02 reconstructed flow.</figcaption></figure><figure class="figure-tile"><a href="cases/boston-assignment.md#physical-link-flow-maps"><img src="assets/boston/assignment_methods_r1/boston_abs_planned_l3_rank52_flow.png" alt="Accepted native L3 rank-52 reconstructed physical-link flow with same scale."></a><figcaption><b>Native L3 · rank 52</b>Outer-02 reconstructed flow.</figcaption></figure></div>
<div class="visual-grid assignment-diff"><figure class="figure-tile"><a href="cases/boston-assignment.md#signed-native-minus-fw-differences"><img src="assets/boston/assignment_methods_r1/boston_abs_planned_l3_rank26_minus_fw.png" alt="Signed native rank-26 minus FW link-flow differences."></a><figcaption><b>Rank 26 − FW</b>Maximum |Δ| = 5.888579437396402e-6 modelled vehicle trips.</figcaption></figure><figure class="figure-tile"><a href="cases/boston-assignment.md#signed-native-minus-fw-differences"><img src="assets/boston/assignment_methods_r1/boston_abs_planned_l3_rank52_minus_fw.png" alt="Signed native rank-52 minus FW link-flow differences on the same zero-centred scale."></a><figcaption><b>Rank 52 − FW</b>Maximum |Δ| = 5.88828736169944e-6 modelled vehicle trips.</figcaption></figure></div>
<p class="focus-note">The three absolute maps share extent, road background, normalization and line width; both signed maps share a zero-centred scale. Near-identical flows are the saved finding, not a reason to amplify differences. These are modelled panel vehicle trips, <b>not GPS counts</b>. The <a href="assets/boston/assignment_methods_r1/boston_abs_planned_assignment_links.csv">full-precision 5,091-row physical-link table</a>, <a href="assets/boston/assignment_methods_r1/BOSTON_ASSIGNMENT_FIGURE_SOURCES.json">field/scale/source manifest</a> and <a href="cases/boston-assignment.md">detailed assignment page</a> provide exact inspection routes.</p>

<div class="soft"><div class="wrap"><section id="sioux-case" class="case-section">
<p class="eyebrow">Case 02 · classical assignment benchmark</p><div class="sectionhead"><h2>Sioux Falls: static FW, native L3 and historical time-expanded CG.</h2><p>The classic demand is exogenous; it is not a new GPS/GTFS or calibrated four-stage city study.</p></div>
<p>The historical <a href="datasets/sioux-static-fw.md">static FW</a> result saved F=<b>4,236,715.140437842</b>, but its retained runtime OD identity is insufficient for an exact same-input native reference claim. The corrected native Diagnostic L3 profile uses a frozen 76-link, 528-positive-OD, 2,218-path instance with rank 50, 585 reduced path coordinates and 661 total native variables. Both selected outer-04 points passed recorded original-space numerical tolerances; their full-network gaps remain nonzero.</p>
<div class="tablewrap"><table><thead><tr><th>Selected native run</th><th>Gamma</th><th>Original Beckmann component F</th><th>Max OD residual</th><th>Full-network relative cost gap</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><a href="../examples/sioux-falls/native_l3_r1/runs/SiouxFalls/A_REG001/outer_04_check.json">A_REG001 · outer 04</a></td><td>0.01</td><td>4,325,864.946597109</td><td>5.548833712509804e-7</td><td><b>8.167461%</b></td></tr><tr><td><a href="../examples/sioux-falls/native_l3_r1/runs/SiouxFalls/B_BECKMANN/outer_04_check.json">B_BECKMANN · outer 04</a></td><td>0</td><td>4,289,674.484214505</td><td>6.957361051718181e-7</td><td><b>4.381867%</b></td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p class="note">A includes reference-centred regularization and B is unregularized; F is only the original Beckmann component. Neither result is a full-network UE certificate or new empirical validation. The 200OD/250OD figures above are historical <b>finite time-expanded CG</b> on different selected-link/horizon instances, not this static native input.</p>
